tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Non Payment of IGST of Rs. 1,04,61,697 on import of Rs. 5,81,20,541 - Non-payment of GST amounting to Rs. 12,78,900/- on Corporate Guarantee given to subsidiary companies - Mis-match in ITC availed in GSTR 2A and 3B resulting in excess utilization of ITC amounting to Rs. 20,01,250/- - Wrong availment/utilization of ineligible credit in TRAN-1 return amounting to Rs. 16,20,569/- Rs. 1,53,63,416 GST + 1,53,63,416 Penalty Rs. 3,07,25,832

In pursuance of audit undertaken for the F.Y. 2021-22, it is observed from books of accounts and returns filed on GST Portal, that the taxpayer has received inward supply from M/S SHILPKAR (INDIA) PVT LTD. GSTIN- 05AACCS1738A1ZX as pre-fabricated building (narrations in invoice as “supply of pre-fabricated for building for project office as per layout plan of specific size as per drawing”). Such pre-fabricated building is tent amounts to be civil structure as it is permanently fastened to the earth as revealed by the examination of actual site where such building is attached to the earth as the normal building having permanent fixtures with facilities of office furnishings, safety tank, light and water facility etc. Such structure is surrounded by the support of inter locking with well-developed surroundings of garden, boundary wall, locked gate etc. The wrongly availed and utilized Input tax credit amounting to Rs. 44,26,405/- which is recoverable from the taxpayer u/s 73 of The RGST/CGST Act along with applicable interest under section 50(1) of The RGST/CGST Act, 2017 r/w section 20 of The IGST Act, 2017 Interest of Rs. 28,81,407 Penalty of Rs. 4,42,641
tax_litigation.status: Appeal has beeen filed against the order

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: As per the Hon’ble Supreme Court judgment in the case of Cosmo Films Ltd. [TS-162-SC-2023-GST] upholding the validity of pre-import condition that all the imports made under the AA scheme on or after 13 October 2017 and up to and including 9 January 2019 which could not meet the pre-import condition may be regularised by making payment of IGST and GST Compensation Cess (Cess) along with the procedure for making payment of IGST and Cess and its consequential claim of input tax credit/refund. The company had received a show cause notice from DRI Kolkata dated 03.10.2019 that it has breached the pre-import condition and is liable to pay a duty of 8.15 Cr. The matter got centralised and Commissioner of Customs (Adjudication) , Mumbai had been appointed as adjudicating Authority to adjudicate this issue. The company had made the details of all bill of entries and shipping bills falling under the 6 advance authorisation Licences which were subject matter under the impugned SCN. In the personnel hearing with Commissioner of Customs (Adjudication), the company Suo-Motto accepted the fact that in case of 8 bill of entries the company has breached the pre-import condition and given its consent to deposit the IGST of Rs 18,42,165/- on immediate basis and requested the waiver of interest and penalty on the same. However, Commissioner of Customs (Adjudication) passed an order by demanding Custom duty of INR INR 8,15,09,369/- and also Imposed a fine of INR 2,25,00,000/- and penalty of Rs. 80,00,000/-. The company has Filed appeal before Customs, Central Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal, Mumbai Appeal Number C/87026/2024-CU[DB]
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Customs, Central Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal, Mumbai

timeline.summary: DEE Development reported an order book of ₹1,909.82 Cr for April 2026 alongside ₹211 Cr in L1 bids.

DEE Development Engineers Limited scheduled an earnings conference call on **May 22, 2026, at 05:00 PM IST** to discuss Q4 & FY2026 performance, led by **Mr. Krishan Lalit Bansal (Chairman & Managing Director)** and **Mr. Brham Prakash Yadav (CFO)**.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹361.57 Cr, net profit to shareholders ₹28.01 Cr.

DEE Development's material subsidiary DEE Piping System (Thailand) signed a Reservation Agreement with an undisclosed international EPC company for 60% of its HRSG pipe spool fabrication capacity, June 2027 to December 2029, at a minimum of US$ 15.27 million a year.
Ranjan Kumar Sarangi hosted an earnings call on May 22, 2026, to discuss DEE Development Engineers Limited’s audited financial results for Q4FY26 and FY26.
DEE Development Engineers Limited resubmitted the audio recording link for its 22 May 2026 earnings call on 23 May 2026 due to a technical error.
DEE Development's Q4/FY26 call (22 May 2026) guided FY27 order inflow above ₹2,000 Cr; revenue of ₹1,500 Cr and consolidated EBITDA margin above 19%
On May 30, 2026, DEE Development Engineers announced securing piping supply contracts worth ₹386.86 Cr (including GST) from Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd, to be executed by February 2028.

On 2 June 2026, DEE Development Engineers said it received a Letter of Intent worth ₹206.55 Cr (excluding GST) from an undisclosed public sector Maharatna power EPC for critical piping assembly, to be executed 6-15 months from purchase order.
On June 3, 2026, DEE Development Engineers approved a preferential issue of equity shares worth ₹300 Cr at ₹502 per share to promoters and institutional investors.
On 8 June 2026, DEE Development Engineers reported May 2026 order inflow of ₹107.83 Cr and execution of ₹631.91 Cr, lifting the closing order book to ₹2,433.90 Cr from ₹1,909.82 Cr.
15 Oct 2026: DEE Development said it secured contracts worth about ₹46 Cr from a US EPC company for modules and off-skid piping fabrication, delivery by July 2027.

16 Oct 2026: DEE Development signed a framework agreement with an unnamed domestic EPC contractor to jointly pursue nuclear power piping business (PHWR, LWR, SMR), with no committed order value or execution period.
